gao-gaoreports-gao-08-277t: This 2007 Government Accountability Office testimony addresses the fund that pays for decontaminating and decommissioning old uranium enrichment plants. GAO warns that the fund's authorization may need to be extended to cover projected cleanup costs, which were expected to outlast the money available. The report lays out the cost projections behind the warning and the stakes of letting the fund run dry.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-227t: A 2007 Government Accountability Office update on the Capitol Visitor Center, the long-delayed underground complex beneath the U.S. Capitol. The testimony reports on the project's schedule and cost status as of October 31, 2007, tracking yet another round of overruns on a project Congress itself oversaw. The findings capture a federal construction saga familiar to anyone who follows how Washington builds.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-207t: In 2007 testimony, the Government Accountability Office reported that the VA and Defense Department kept expanding their sharing of medical information but still lacked comprehensive electronic health records. For service members moving between military and veterans' care, the gap meant records didn't follow patients. GAO's findings spotlighted a problem both departments had promised to fix for years — with billions spent and no unified record to show.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-177t: GAO briefed Congress in 2007 on the war against fakes and rip-offs — knockoff goods, pirated code, and stolen trade secrets bleeding U.S. firms dry. The briefing maps how the federal piracy cops were lined up and where the coverage thinned. It is a snapshot of the knockoff fight just before the web turned it into a flood.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-97t: GAO took Congress inside Florida's vanished-vote mystery in 2007 — the House race where thousands of ballots seemed to melt. Tests on the voting gear could raise trust in the outcome, GAO said, but never fully prove it. The briefing is a sober lesson in the limits of forensics when the machines ate the evidence.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1257t: Nobody was clearly driving the flu-response bus in 2007, GAO told Congress — too many agencies held pieces of the wheel. The briefing urges sharp lines of command and tighter outbreak plans before a real pandemic tests them. History would grade this warning as one of the watchdog's most prophetic.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1247t: The next-gen bomb sniffers for the border had to prove themselves first, GAO told Congress in 2007. Radiation gates that miss are worse than none — they breed false comfort. The briefing demands road-tested proof before the nation bets its nuclear tripwires on shiny new gear.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1167t: Florida's ghost-vote saga got a status check in 2007 — GAO briefed Congress mid-probe on its review of the 13th District's voting gear. The testimony previews the forensic hunt without tipping the verdict. The briefing kept the pressure on for answers in a race the machines may have swallowed.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1137t: Dead farmers were getting farm checks in 2007 — GAO told Congress the farm agency needed tighter locks against bad payments to estates and trusts. The briefing exposes the subsidy leaks in plain numbers. The findings demand basic bookkeeping discipline: verify the living, and do not pay the departed.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1107t: Iraq's oil lifeline was choking in 2007 — GAO's briefing says graft and violence crippled efforts to revive the petroleum sector and pass the oil law. The testimony ties black gold to the war's outcome. The findings warn that a broke oil state cannot fund its own peace.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1097t: Foster kids aging out needed a launchpad in 2007 — GAO's briefing says federal action could help states ready them for solo life. The testimony presses for better bridges to adulthood. The findings argue that the system raising these kids owes them more than a goodbye at eighteen.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1047t: Foreign students were looking elsewhere in 2007 — GAO's briefing says America was losing its pull on international scholars, with global stakes. The testimony links campus visas to national competitiveness. The findings warn that the world's best minds would simply go where they were wanted.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-897t: June brought another verse of the Capitol basement saga in 2007 — GAO's briefing logs the Visitor Center's latest schedule and cost. The testimony's refrain was familiar: later, pricier. The findings kept Congress's own project under the microscope it aimed at others.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-997t: Hiring an army of border agents was pricey in 2007 — GAO's briefing breaks down the costs and headaches of training the surge. The testimony puts numbers to the hiring wave. The findings ask whether the rush to staff the line was building quality or just quantity.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-827t: Iraq's friends were asked to pay up in 2007 — GAO's briefing tallies coalition help and donor pledges for the rebuild effort. The testimony follows the promised money to see what arrived. The findings ask whether the world put its wallets where its resolutions were.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-777t: Teaching America about money was floundering in 2007 — GAO's briefing says the financial-literacy commission needed to get serious about a national strategy. The testimony grades the effort. The findings' verdict: good intentions, thin results, and a nation still bad at budgets.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-797t: A rocket-fuel chemical was showing up in drinking water in 2007 — GAO's briefing says the EPA did not even track perchlorate pollution incidents in any systematic way. The testimony exposes the monitoring gap in plain terms. The findings warn that the uncounted pollutant is the uncontrolled one, and the public drinks the difference.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-727t: Missile defense needed both speed and honesty in 2007 — GAO's briefing says the program wanted a better mix of freedom and clear answers. The testimony walks the fine line with great care. The findings warn that agility without accountability is just pricey improvisation.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-687t: The anthrax sniffers could not be trusted in 2007 — GAO's briefing says Homeland Security could not prove its sampling would actually work. The testimony delivers the scary verdict. The findings' bottom line is chilling: the bio-attack alarm might simply not ring.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-617t: The airport-funding formula was up for debate in 2007 — GAO's briefing gives an early read on the proposed program changes. The testimony previews the stakes. The findings ask which runways the new math would pave, and which it would skip.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-637t: Iraq's security ministries were a budget swamp in 2007, and GAO's briefing previews the money and management troubles in full detail. The testimony sketches the dysfunction for Congress. The findings warn that the ministries holding the guns could not even count their own cash.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-587t: Medicare doctors were dodging their own taxes in 2007, and GAO's briefing says thousands of providers abused the federal tax system. The testimony names the scandal outright for Congress. The findings' sting is sharp: the healers paid by the Treasury would not pay the Treasury.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-607t: Uncle Sam's own books were still unauditable in 2007, and GAO's briefing says sustained improvement in federal financial management was needed. The testimony delivers the embarrassing verdict. The findings' shame is plain: the world's biggest budget could not pass an audit.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-547t: The watchdog passed its own hat again in 2007, with GAO's briefing laying out the coming year's budget request. The testimony justifies the dollars line by line for Congress. The findings show the auditor practicing its own transparency sermon, as it should.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-567t: Studying doctors' habits could tame Medicare spending in 2007, and GAO's briefing previews an approach built on physician practice patterns. The testimony makes the data case clearly. The findings bet that measuring medicine carefully will improve medicine. The data would do the talking.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-507t: February brought the usual grim update on the Capitol's basement project in 2007, and GAO's briefing logs the Visitor Center's schedule and cost. The testimony's refrain stayed bleak. The findings kept the microscope on Congress's own money pit. The basement project was Congress's own embarrassment.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-497t: Health care spending was swallowing budgets in 2007, and GAO's briefing says public payers bore the entitlement burden while all payers faced rising prices. The testimony maps the squeeze. The findings warn that the medical bill was outgrowing the nation's wallet.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-447t: States' experience with kids' health insurance got a GAO review in 2007, and the briefing covers the SCHIP rollout and reauthorization stakes. The testimony previews the fight. The findings ask whether the children's program would survive the politics. The coverage hung in the balance.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-427t: Wildfire spending was burning out of control in 2007, and GAO's briefing says the lack of a cohesive strategy hobbled cost containment. The testimony demands the plan. The findings warn that the flames were outpacing the firefighting budgets. The strategy had to catch up to the smoke.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-397t: The Pentagon's people plan did not match its war plan in 2007, and GAO's briefing says the department needed a better link between strategy and personnel needs. The testimony demands the connection. The findings warn that the strategy was only as strong as its staffing. The troops had to fit the mission.
